solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Unvaried sound not found in satellite echo

indicators.note: the word not is found sitting inside the satellite word, so it is put inside

parts.note: the Moon is Earth's natural satellite
Echo is E in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A dull tone missing from a signal bounced back by a satellite.
explanation.definitionFit: A monotone is a single unchanging pitch of voice or sound, hence an unvaried sound.

clue.text: Concerned with now ended meal

parts.note: re means concerning or with regard to
something now ended is past

explanation.surface: Someone talks about a dinner that has just finished.
explanation.definitionFit: A repast is a formal or literary word for a meal.

clue.text: Tea, say, always carried in item of luggage with English

indicators.note: the word for always is carried inside the luggage word, so it is put inside

parts.note: a bag is an item of luggage
ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'

explanation.surface: A traveller always packs some English tea in their bag.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea is an example of a drink, and 'say' flags that it is one instance of a beverage.

clue.text: Sudden flood cut short argument

indicators.note: a word cut short loses its final letter, here the end of the flood word

parts.note: a spate is a sudden flood of water

explanation.surface: A flash flood brings a row to an abrupt end.
explanation.definitionFit: A spat is a petty quarrel, a minor argument.

clue.text: One who forbids the use of flag

definitions.text: One who forbids the use of
definitions.meaning: a ..., read cryptically, is someone who bans things
a flag or long strip of cloth bearing a slogan

explanation.surface: A censor who outlaws the flying of flags.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the agent noun from ban; the other is the ordinary cloth standard carried in processions.

clue.text: Quote view delivered in speech

indicators.note: words delivered in speech are heard rather than seen, so the answer sounds like the view word

parts.note: a sight is a view or something seen

explanation.surface: A speaker quotes their opinion in an address.
explanation.definitionFit: To cite is to quote a passage or author as authority.

clue.text: Sleep with at least 24, but no Poles

indicators.note: no tells us to drop the two poles from the longer word

parts.note: dozens means at least two lots of twelve, so 24 or more
the Poles are N and S, north and south

explanation.surface: A puzzling instruction about sleeping with two dozen or more but no Polish people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' with its capital suggests people from Poland, but it means the magnetic poles, N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: To doze is to sleep lightly.

clue.text: Stress European parliamentarian has one son

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one
S is the standard abbreviation for son, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: An MEP from Europe is under strain because of family worries.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphasis is stress placed on a word or idea to mark its importance.

clue.text: Thus fortify with alcohol for consolation

parts.note: so means thus, in this way
to lace a drink is to spike or fortify it with spirits

explanation.surface: Spiking a drink as a way to cheer someone up.
explanation.definitionFit: Solace is comfort given in distress, a synonym of consolation.

clue.text: Christmas decoration can seem extremely large initially

parts.note: a tin is a can, as for food

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letters of the three words that follow can

explanation.surface: A festive ornament may look enormous at first glance.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinsel is glittering metallic strands hung on trees as Christmas decoration.

clue.text: Force to retreat right away from home

parts.note: out means not at home, as in 'she is out'

explanation.surface: A sports team drives back opponents in an away match.
explanation.definitionFit: To rout an army is to defeat it and drive it into disorderly flight.

clue.text: Correct account given by clergyman

parts.note: a curate is an assistant clergyman in a parish

explanation.surface: A churchman gives a truthful version of events.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate means free from error, which is a synonym of correct as an adjective.

clue.text: Disaster with area hit hard in major town

indicators.note: in places the area and hitting words inside the town word

parts.note: a city is a major town
to lam is to thrash or hit hard

explanation.surface: A catastrophe strikes a large area of a big town.
explanation.definitionFit: A calamity is an event causing great damage or distress, a synonym of disaster.

clue.text: Having a shower perhaps after time working out

indicators.note: after places the weather word after the time letter in the answer

parts.note: raining is what the sky does in a shower, 'perhaps' because a shower is only one kind

explanation.surface: Someone takes a shower after time spent at the gym.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having a shower' suggests washing after exercise, but here it is the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Training is physical exercise or practice, which is what working out means as a noun phrase.

clue.text: Disordered exercises left learner and me with lines

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises
L is for learner, as on British learner-driver plates
taken as written
LL is the abbreviation for lines, a single L being a line

explanation.surface: A messy gym session involving a novice, the speaker and some queues.
explanation.definitionFit: Pell-mell means in a confused, disorderly rush.

clue.text: What's blocked movement to cut down trees and conserve

parts.note: to log is to fell trees for timber
conserve is a noun meaning jam or preserve

explanation.surface: Something stopped the work of felling trees and protecting forests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conserve' reads as a verb about protecting forests but is the noun meaning preserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A logjam is a mass of floating logs stopping a river's flow, and by extension any blockage of progress.

clue.text: Fine and soft plant fibres

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
lax means slack or soft, not strict

explanation.surface: Describing delicate, gentle threads from a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Flax is a plant whose stem fibres are spun into linen thread.

clue.text: Horse and cattle fodder adapted to season

parts.note: for means suited or adapted to, as in 'designed for'
season and age both mean a period of time

explanation.surface: Animal feed is adjusted according to the time of year.
explanation.definitionFit: Forage is food such as hay or grass for horses and cattle.

clue.text: Insult succeeded with brilliance

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in family trees
brilliance is brightness, or light

explanation.surface: A cutting remark landed well because it was so clever.
explanation.definitionFit: A slight is a snub or insult, from treating someone as of little account.

clue.text: Full opera needs cutting down for run

indicators.note: the two words need trimming at both ends, leaving the run of letters sitting inside them

explanation.surface: A full-length opera is too long and needs shortening to run.
explanation.walkthrough: The run of letters lies inside 'Full opera' across the word break.
explanation.definitionFit: To lope is to run with long, easy strides.

clue.text: Accept post when head is sacked

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, sacked meaning removed

parts.note: a stake is a post driven into the ground

explanation.surface: Taking a job after the boss has been fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'post' suggests a job and 'head is sacked' a boss fired, but post is a wooden stake.
explanation.definitionFit: To take an offer is to accept it.

clue.text: Airman crashing in harbour

indicators.note: crashing suggests the airman's letters smashed and scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A pilot crash-lands in a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A marina is a harbour built for yachts and small pleasure boats.

clue.text: Wild puma trek appealing to the affluent traveller?

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of puma trek running loose into a new order

explanation.surface: A wild-cat safari is a luxury holiday aimed at wealthy tourists.
explanation.definitionFit: Upmarket means aimed at wealthier, more discerning customers; the query notes the puma trek as one such trip.

clue.text: Game no good: yet medal results

parts.note: Go is a Japanese board game

explanation.surface: A useless match still ends with someone being decorated.
explanation.definitionFit: Gong is informal British slang for a medal or award.
